subject: SIG: clarification on prompt/log retention and training exceptions
messages:
From: Julie Patel <julie.patel@greenwellhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: SIG clarifications: prompts/logs and training usage

Hi Markus,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec team: we need a concise, written confirmation on two points for our procurement file and the security review board:

1) Retention: what is your retention policy for request/response logs and KV/prefix caches (typical TTLs, any circumstances data is stored longer)?
2) Training: do you ever use customer prompt content, responses, or logs to train or improve models (including internal research unless explicitly contracted)? If so, please describe opt-in/opt-out controls and evidence.

Can you provide a short paragraph we can include in our SIG evidence package and attach SOC 2 or other artifacts? Also any diagrams showing where logs flow (control plane vs. private deployments).

Thanks — Julie
Julie Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, Greenwell Health
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Julie Patel <julie.patel@greenwellhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG clarifications: prompts/logs and training usage

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a redwood_SIG_answers_v1.pdf and our SOC 2 report for your folder. Neha and Priyom are on-copy and will supply the diagram and the more formal language you can include in the SIG evidence package.

1) Retention: For hosted API (Redwood Cloud) transient request/response logs and inference traces are retained for billing, telemetry, and abuse detection. Default retention is 30 days for full request/response artifacts and 90 days for aggregated usage metrics. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments control storage retention in their environment; Redwood does not access private-deployment request logs unless explicitly granted.

2) Training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, responses, or request logs from customer accounts to train or improve models by default. Training on customer-provided data happens only under explicit, documented opt-in agreements (contract addendum) and with signed data processing terms; such projects are tracked, scoped, and restricted to separate controlled datasets.

Evidence included: SOC 2 Type II (controls around data access), SIG answers PDF, and a network/data flow diagram (shared link).

If you need a single-sentence attestation for a procurement checklist we can provide: "Redwood Inference does not utilize customer request or response data for model training unless the customer has provided explicit, documented consent via contract addendum; hosted logs are retained for 30 days by default for billing and fraud detection, with aggregated metrics retained up to 90 days. Dedicated and Private deployments are customer-controlled and not used for training by Redwood unless otherwise contracted."

Let us know if you'd like this on company letterhead or an executed attestation.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Julie — adding a couple of technical clarifications for the SIG Evidence folder and linking a diagram. See the short bullets you can paste directly into the SIG: 

• Hosted (Redwood Cloud): raw request/response payloads are stored in an encrypted S3-backed store for 30 days by default to support billing, diagnostics, and abuse detection. Access to raw artifacts is limited to a small number of SRE and security engineers and is audited (see SOC 2 control ID in attached report). Aggregated, de-identified usage metrics are retained for up to 90 days.

• Dedicated: logs reside in the customer's dedicated capacity. By default Redwood does not read or export those logs. Retention is configurable by the customer.

• Private (VPC/on-prem): all data handling is governed by the customer's infrastructure and KMS; Redwood's control plane only stores metadata necessary for orchestration and is configurable.

• Training: customer account data (prompts/responses/attachments) is never used for model training unless there is a documented opt-in and a signed SOW/amendment. Any approved training projects use segregated datasets, access-controlled pipelines, and are subject to an internal approval checklist and external documentation for customers.

Attachments: redwood_SIG_answers_v1.pdf (short answers you can paste), data_flow_diagram.png (control/data plane diagram), SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf (control evidence).

On a related note, if Greenwell requires an executed attestation we can route that through Legal — let me know and I'll start the workflow.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Markus/Neha — this is exactly what we need. Two quick clarifications before we close out: 

1) Can you confirm the default 30-day retention applies to request bodies including any user-supplied files/attachments sent to the API?
2) For hosted accounts, is there a mechanism for customers to request immediate deletion of raw artifacts (prior to 30 days) and how quickly is that processed?

If you can reply with 1–2 lines addressing those, we can finalize the SIG and move the deal to legal.

Best,
Julie
Senior Procurement Manager, Greenwell Health
